# php-via: Full LLM Reference

**Version**: 0.14.1 (MIT) | **Requires**: PHP 8.4+, ext-openswoole 26
**Install**: `composer require mbolli/php-via`, plus `composer require twig/twig` for Twig templates
**Homepage**: https://via.zweiundeins.gmbh/
**GitHub**: https://github.com/mbolli/php-via
**Packagist**: https://packagist.org/packages/mbolli/php-via
**Upgrading from 0.13**: https://via.zweiundeins.gmbh/docs/upgrading
**Author**: Michael Bolli <michael@bolli.us>

---

## What is php-via?

php-via is a real-time reactive web framework for PHP. It runs as a persistent
OpenSwoole server that keeps a long-lived SSE (Server-Sent Events) connection to every
browser tab. When state changes on the server, it pushes HTML and signal patches to the
connected tabs, and Datastar (1.0.4, served by php-via) morphs them into the page. No
JavaScript to write, no build step, multiplayer by default.

The name "via" means "the way". From one PHP process you get server-pushed real-time
updates without WebSockets, polling or a frontend framework.

---

## Architecture Overview

```
Browser ──── GET /page ────────────────► RequestHandler  (creates Context, renders HTML)
Browser ──── GET /_sse ────────────────► SseHandler      (long-lived stream, sends patches)
Browser ──── POST /_action/:id ────────► ActionHandler   (writes posted signals, runs the action)
                                              │
                                         Application
                                         ├── Router        (route matching, reflection DI)
                                         ├── Context       (per tab: signals, actions, views)
                                         │   ├── PatchManager   (Channel → SSE queue)
                                         │   ├── SignalFactory
                                         │   ├── ComponentManager (sub-contexts)
                                         │   └── ContextLifecycle (timers, tasks, cleanup)
                                         ├── Broadcast flush (per worker, once per tick)
                                         └── Broker        (InMemory / Swoole / Redis / NATS)
```

**Public API surface**: `Via`, `Context`, `Signal`, `Action`, `Scope`, `Config`, plus `PatchMode`,
`ErrorPhase`, `Testing\TestApp`, `Rendering\TemplateEngine` and `Twig\TwigEngine`.

---

## Getting Started

### Requirements

- PHP 8.4 or higher
- OpenSwoole extension 26 (`pecl install openswoole-26.2.0`)
- Composer
- Optional: `twig/twig` 3.10+ for Twig templates
- Optional: `ext-brotli`: static files get Brotli level 11 once it is loaded, pages and SSE with `withBrotli()`

### Installation

```bash
composer require mbolli/php-via
composer require twig/twig   # for Twig templates (withTemplateDir()); closure views need nothing more
```

### Minimal counter app (complete working example)

```php
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

require __DIR__ . '/vendor/autoload.php';

use Mbolli\PhpVia\Config;
use Mbolli\PhpVia\Context;
use Mbolli\PhpVia\Via;

$app = new Via(new Config());

$app->page('/', function (Context $c): void {
    $count = $c->signal(0, 'count');

    $increment = $c->action(function () use ($count): void {
        $count->setValue($count->int() + 1); // sent to the tab when the action ends
    }, 'increment');

    $c->view(fn (): string => <<<HTML
        <main id="counter">
            <p data-text="{$count->ref()}">{$count->int()}</p>
            <button data-on:click="@post('{$increment->url()}')">+1</button>
        </main>
    HTML);
});

$app->start(); // http://localhost:3000
```

---

## Core Concepts

### 1. Signals

Signals are reactive PHP values scoped to a tab, a route, a session, the whole server or a
custom group. Their values are sent to the browser's Datastar store and kept in sync.

```php
// Every signal needs a name; without a scope it is private to the tab
$count  = $c->signal(0, 'count');        // integer
$name   = $c->signal('', 'name');        // string
$active = $c->signal(false, 'active');   // bool
$items  = $c->signal([], 'items');       // array → JSON
$votes  = $c->signal(0, 'votes', Scope::ROUTE);              // shared by every tab on this route
$quiet  = $c->signal(0, 'quiet', Scope::GLOBAL, autoBroadcast: false); // shared, never broadcasts by itself

// Read values (typed)
$count->int();
$name->string();
$active->bool();   // strings via filter_var, other values by PHP truthiness
$items->array();
$count->getValue(); // mixed, raw

// Write. A scoped signal schedules a broadcast of its scope (unless autoBroadcast: false).
$count->setValue(42);
$count->markSynced();   // the tab already shows this value: send no patch for it

// Shared counters and lists: update without losing writes from other workers
$votes->increment();                                   // atomic, returns the new value
$items->mutate(fn (array $list) => [...$list, $item]); // read-modify-write under a lock

// Datastar references
$count->id();          // the id the browser uses
$count->ref();         // '$' . id, for data-text and other expressions
$count->bind();        // data-bind="<id>"
$count->bind('value'); // data-bind__prop.value="<id>", for web components
```

`setValue()`, `increment()` and `mutate()` take no flags: `broadcast:` and `markChanged:`
throw an `ArgumentCountError`. Declare `autoBroadcast: false` for a quiet scoped signal, and
call `markSynced()` after a write the tab already shows. Render a value with
`<span data-text="{$s->ref()}">{$s->string()}</span>`.

**Ids**: a signal's id is unique per tab and includes the tab for TAB signals, so always
write it from the signal object: `id()`, `ref()`, `bind()` in PHP, or `{{ count.id }}`,
`{{ count.ref }}` in Twig. A scoped signal outside a component keeps a readable id when its
name is letters and digits and its scope is letters and digits joined by `:` or a route of
such segments: `global_count`, `room_lobby_online` for `room:lobby`, `route___likes` for
`route:/`. Every other id ends in `____` plus codes. SESSION signal ids carry a hash of the session id. To find a scoped
signal from code outside a context (a timer), use `$app->getScopedSignalByName($scope, $name)`
with a resolved scope such as `Scope::routeScope('/board')`.

**Who may write a signal from the browser**: Datastar posts every signal with each action.
By default TAB signals take the posted value and scoped signals are server-owned.
`clientWritable: true` or `false` on `signal()` (or `#[Signal]`) overrides this for any
scope, and `Config::withStrictTabSignals()` makes TAB signals server-owned by default.
A posted value must have the type of the signal's initial value; lossless strings convert
(`'5'` to 5, `'false'` to false), anything else is refused. A signal declared with `null`
takes any type.

**Browser-owned initial value**: `$c->signal($fallback, 'name', clientSeeded: true)` declares
a TAB signal whose value the browser holds first (declared on `<html>` or in `<head>` before
`via_head`): the page seed leaves it out, and every SSE connect gives it the browser's value
before the view renders, until the server writes it.

### 2. Actions

Actions are server-side handlers registered on a context and called from the browser with a
Datastar expression such as `@post(...)`. An action runs for the tab that posts it.

```php
$inc = $c->action(function (Context $c) use ($count): void {
    $count->setValue($count->int() + 1);
}, 'increment');

$inc->url(); // "/_action/increment"

// In HTML: <button data-on:click="@post('/_action/increment')">+1</button>

// Signal values the browser posts are written into the signals before the action runs
$greet = $c->action(function (Context $c) use ($name, $greeting): void {
    $greeting->setValue('Hello ' . $name->string());
}, 'greet');

// Read input that is not a signal (POST body or query string)
$c->action(function (Context $c): void {
    $option = $c->input('option');
}, 'vote');
```

After an action, php-via sends the signals it changed to its tab, also when it throws, for the
page and its components. A trailing `syncSignals()` is not needed. Call `$c->sync()` to
re-render the view. Keep `syncSignals()` in timers, `spawn()` tasks and hooks, and for
scoped signals declared `autoBroadcast: false`. `action()` takes two arguments: a third
(the removed scope) throws an `ArgumentCountError`.

An action that throws answers 500 `Action failed`; the worker keeps running, the error is
logged and goes to `$app->onError()`. Registering a second TAB action under the same name
replaces the first with a warning.

Each action reads its own request: `input()`, `file()`, `cookie()` and
`getRequestAttribute()` return the values of the request that posted it, and a cookie from
`setCookie()`, like the new session cookie of `regenerateSession()`, goes out with that
action's response, also when two actions of one tab run at once. A `spawn()` task keeps the
request of its action, but `file()` is null once the action has answered (OpenSwoole deletes
the temporary file). Code outside an action, such as a timer, reads the page request, and a
cookie it sets goes out with the tab's next action response. On a page load `input()` reads
the query string. Signals are tab state: an action that waits sees values a later action
posted.

Datastar cancels an in-flight request when the page sends another one with the same method
and URL, from any element. A request cancelled before it reaches the server never runs its
action. Where every request counts, or two elements post the same action for different
reasons, give each a query string or turn cancellation off:

```html
<button data-on:click="@post('/_action/send?from=button')">Send</button>
<button data-on:click="@post('/_action/paint', {requestCancellation: 'disabled'})">Paint</button>
```

### 3. Views

Views render a context's HTML. They run on page load, on `$c->sync()`, on every SSE connect
and on every broadcast flush that reaches the context.

```php
// view(callable|string $view, array|callable $data = [], ?string $block = null, bool $shareRender = false, bool|string $viewTransition = false)

// Closure view returning HTML
$c->view(fn (): string => '<p id="hello">Hello</p>');

// Twig template (needs twig/twig); the context's signals and actions are passed in by name
$c->view('pages/home.html.twig', ['title' => 'Home']);

// Only send a named block on SSE updates
$c->view('page.html.twig', block: 'counter');

// Data read on every render, for values that change after page load
$c->view('presence.html.twig', fn (): array => ['count' => $app->countClients(Scope::GLOBAL)]);

// One render per broadcast for every tab in the primary scope (only for views identical for all tabs)
$c->scope(Scope::ROUTE);
$c->view('board.html.twig', fn (): array => ['cells' => $board->cells()], block: 'board', shareRender: true);
```

A string is always a template name: a string of HTML throws, and so does a callable view
with `$data` or `block:`. Every view renders per tab unless it passes `shareRender: true`,
which needs a shared primary scope set with `scope()` (on a TAB-primary context it throws)
and is ignored for a view that renders a whole document. The shared render is keyed by scope,
route pattern and component. Never share a view that shows TAB signals, per-user data or
components.

Pass changing data as a closure, as above. An array computed in the page handler is frozen
at page load.

`viewTransition: true` applies each update inside a view transition, and a CSS selector scopes
it to that element. The page load and the render on SSE connect have none. Leave it off for
views that update several times a second: a document transition's overlay takes the clicks
while it runs.

Every update, and every SSE connect and reconnect, morphs the view into the page, which sets
each element's attributes to the server's markup. An attribute the browser set itself, such
as the `open` that `showModal()` puts on a `<dialog>`, would go, so list it in
`data-preserve-attr` in the rendered markup:

```html
<dialog id="confirm" data-preserve-attr="open">...</dialog>
```

Outside the view:

```php
use Mbolli\PhpVia\PatchMode;

$c->patchElements('<li>new row</li>', '#log', PatchMode::Append); // Outer and Replace need no selector
$c->patchElements(selector: '#toast', mode: PatchMode::Remove);
$c->patchElements('<div id="toast">Saved</div>', viewTransition: true); // or a selector to scope it
$c->dispatch('toast', ['text' => 'Saved']);   // CustomEvent on window: data-on:toast__window="..."
$c->execScript('console.log("hi")');
$c->isConnected();                            // the tab's stream is open on this worker
```

### 4. Scopes

Scope controls which contexts share signals and receive broadcasts together.

| Scope | Who shares state |
|---|---|
| `Scope::TAB` (default) | Fully isolated per browser tab |
| `Scope::ROUTE` | All tabs on the same route |
| `Scope::SESSION` | All tabs of one browser session (each session has its own scope) |
| `Scope::GLOBAL` | Every connected client |
| `"room:lobby"` | Custom string, any group you define |
| `"room:*"` | Wildcard, matches all `room:…` scopes |

```php
// Primary scope of the context: what its view shares and $c->broadcast() reaches
$c->scope(Scope::ROUTE);
$c->scope('room:' . $roomId);

// A shared signal names its scope; after scope() a signal without one throws
$c->signal(0, 'count', Scope::ROUTE);
$c->signal('', 'draft', Scope::TAB);

// Join a second scope to receive its broadcasts (a scoped signal joins by itself)
$c->addScope('room:lobby');

// Broadcast to a scope from anywhere
$app->broadcast(Scope::GLOBAL);
$app->broadcast(Scope::routeScope('/dashboard'));        // one route
$app->broadcast(Scope::sessionScope($c->getSessionId())); // one session
$app->broadcast('room:lobby');
$app->countClients('room:lobby');                        // connected tabs it reaches, every worker

// Broadcast the context's own primary scope; on a TAB-primary context, only this tab
$c->broadcast();

// Push this tab only (no broadcast)
$c->sync();
```

`scope()`, `addScope()`, `removeScope()`, `signal()` and `#[Action(scope: ...)]` resolve
`Scope::ROUTE` and `Scope::SESSION` to this route's and this session's scope. `scope()`
replaces only the primary scope and keeps the scopes the context joined. A bare
`Scope::ROUTE`, `Scope::SESSION` or `Scope::TAB` passed to `$app->broadcast()`,
`$app->countClients()` or `$app->getScopedSignalByName()` throws.

### 5. Components

Components are isolated sub-contexts inside a page. Each has its own signals, actions and
view. Calling the component returns its HTML, already wrapped in a `<div id="c-…">` that
php-via targets with the component's own patches. The namespace is required, unique on its
page, and made of letters, digits, `_` and `-`.

```php
$counter = function (Context $k): void {
    $count = $k->signal(0, 'count');
    $k->action(fn () => $count->setValue($count->int() + 1), 'inc');
    $k->view(fn () => $k->render('components/counter.html.twig')); // count and inc passed in by name
};

$app->page('/dashboard', function (Context $c) use ($counter): void {
    $first = $c->component($counter, 'first');
    $second = $c->component($counter, 'second');

    // Call the components inside the view, so every page render carries their current HTML
    $c->view(fn (): string => $c->render('pages/dashboard.html.twig', [
        'first' => $first(),
        'second' => $second(),
    ]));
});
```

In the template: `{{ first|raw }}`. Do not call a component in the page handler and pass
the string to `$c->view('tpl', [...])`: that HTML is frozen at page load, and every later
page render resets the component. In a loop: `$c->component($row, 'row-' . $id)`.
`$k->getPageContext()` returns the page a component sits on.

### 6. Composition (class-based pages)

```php
use Mbolli\PhpVia\Attributes\Action;
use Mbolli\PhpVia\Attributes\OnCleanup;
use Mbolli\PhpVia\Attributes\Signal;

final class Counter {
    #[Signal] public int $count = 0;                          // TAB
    #[Signal(Scope::ROUTE, atomic: true)] public int $total = 0; // shared, ++ adds across workers

    public function view(Context $ctx): void {
        // Properties are hydrated before each action, and scoped ones before each render
        $ctx->view(fn (): string => '<main id="counter">' . $this->count . ' / ' . $this->total . '</main>');
    }

    #[Action]
    public function increment(Context $ctx): void {
        ++$this->count;
        ++$this->total;
    }

    #[OnCleanup]
    public function bye(Context $ctx): void {}
}

$app->mount(Counter::class, '/counter');
$c->component(VoteWidget::class, 'cats'); // class components need a namespace too
```

In a Twig template the signals arrive by name (`{{ total.int }}`). `#[Broadcast(Scope::ROUTE)]`
on the class sets the primary scope. `#[Action(scope: ...)]`
registers a scoped action, which still runs on the posting tab's own instance; in a component
its URL starts with the namespace (`/_action/cats-vote`). `#[OnDisconnect]` is removed and
throws at `mount()`: use `#[OnCleanup]`, several per class allowed.

---

## Broadcasting

Inside a coroutine (actions, timers, hooks), `broadcast()`, a scoped signal write and a
message from the broker only mark the scope. Each worker flushes the marked scopes once:
at the end of the event-loop turn when it is idle, otherwise at most once per tick
(`Config::withBroadcastTickMs()`, default 25 ms). A flush renders each shared view once,
each other context once, and publishes each scope to the broker once.

What this means for app code:
- Views render the state at flush time. Several writes in one action produce one frame.
- A value set, broadcast and reset within one action never reaches clients.
- Patches the action queues itself (`execScript()`, `$c->sync()`) reach the tab before the
  broadcast frame.
- The action's HTTP response does not wait for the fan-out.
- Under sustained load clients get about one frame per tick and skip the states between.

```php
$app->broadcast(Scope::GLOBAL);   // marks the scope; the flush renders it
$app->flushBroadcasts();          // render the pending flush now, in this coroutine

// At most one render per interval for busy scopes; the last state of a burst always goes out
$config->withBroadcastThrottle('import:*', 250);
```

`Config::withBroadcastCoalescing(false)` is deprecated (removed in 0.15): call
`$app->flushBroadcasts()` where a broadcast has to land first. Outside a coroutine (CLI
scripts, tests) `broadcast()` is synchronous. `$app->getStats()->getBroadcastStats()` reports
flushes, coalesced broadcasts and flush times per worker.

---

## Lifecycle

```php
// Server lifecycle: runs in every worker process, with its id; worker 0 for one-shot work
$app->onWorkerStart(function (int $workerId) use ($app): void { /* ... */ });
$app->onWorkerStop(function (int $workerId) use ($app): void { /* runs on stop, reload and recycle */ });

// Per-client lifecycle
$app->onClientConnect(function (Context $c) use ($app): void {
    $app->broadcast(Scope::routeScope($c->getRoute()));
});
$app->onClientDisconnect(function (Context $c) use ($app): void { /* ... */ });

// Every throw php-via catches from app code: action, render, timer, task or route
$app->onError(function (\Throwable $e, ?Context $c, ErrorPhase $phase, ?string $action): void {
    if ($phase === ErrorPhase::Action && $c !== null) {
        $c->getSignal('error')?->setValue('Failed: ' . $e->getMessage()); // goes out with the 500
    }
});

// Server timer: runs on one worker, once per interval for the whole server
$app->setInterval(function () use ($app): void {
    if ($app->countClients(Scope::GLOBAL) === 0) {
        return;
    }
    $app->broadcast(Scope::GLOBAL);
}, 1000);
$app->setInterval($perProcessWork, 1000, everyWorker: true); // in every worker

// Tab timer: start it in the page handler; it stops with the context
$c->setInterval(fn () => $c->sync(), 1000);

// Work that outlives the action: throws go to onError(), a stopping worker waits for it
$c->spawn(function (Context $c): void {
    $result = runLongQuery();
    if (!$c->isDestroyed()) {
        $c->setTabState('result', $result);
        $c->sync();
    }
});

// Context cleanup hook, when the context is destroyed
$c->onCleanup(function (Context $c): void { /* ... */ });
```

- **A closed tab is noticed at once.** A stream ends about 1 ms after the browser closes
  the connection: `onClientDisconnect` runs, the client leaves `getClients()`, and
  `onCleanup` runs after the cleanup delay (`withContextTimeouts(cleanupDelayMs: ...)`,
  5 s by default).
- **Idle streams stay open behind proxies.** A stream silent for 15 s writes an SSE
  comment (`withSseKeepAliveMs()`, `0` turns it off).
- **SSE needs no proxy setting.** Caddy's `reverse_proxy` flushes `text/event-stream`
  responses immediately, so no `flush_interval` is needed; behind TLS, use
  `reverse_proxy h2c://127.0.0.1:3000` with `withH2c()` for one worker (see Scaling for
  several). The SSE response's `X-Accel-Buffering: no` header turns nginx's proxy buffering
  off for it.
- **A context whose stream never connects is freed** after the connect timeout
  (`withContextTimeouts(connectMs: ...)`, 30 s by default), running its cleanup hooks.
- **An action on a tab whose stream is down keeps it for the reconnect.** The stream
  dropped or the action revived the context: it is freed the reconnect timeout
  (`withContextTimeouts(reconnectMs: ...)`, 60 s by default) after the last action, longer than
  Datastar's 30 s `retryMaxWait`. A context freed before its stream returns drops its
  queued patches; the revived tab gets its signals and a fresh view, not one-off patches.
- **Revival.** A tab that comes back after its context was cleaned up is rebuilt with the
  same id and the signal values it still holds, within the revival window
  (`withContextTimeouts(revivalWindowMs: ...)`, 10 minutes by default), instead of reloading.
  Its page handler runs behind the route's middleware again, on a GET of the page's URL, and
  reads the attributes it and the reviving request's middleware set. `$c->tabState($key)`
  values set with `$c->setTabState($key, $value)` come back; other server-only state such as
  `#[Persist]` starts over. When the route's middleware answers instead, the tab reloads, from
  an SSE reconnect or an action, and the page load gets that answer.
- **Reconnects.** After a network error Datastar retries the stream after 1, 2, 4, 8 and
  16 s, then every 30 s, ten times in all, each time with the tab's current signals. Once
  the retries run out or the stream ends, `via_head` opens a new one within 15 s, and at once
  when the server ends a stream for a session rotation or a stopping worker.

---

## Pages, Routes and Downloads

```php
$app->page('/blog/{slug}', function (Context $c, string $slug): void { /* ... */ }); // decoded params
$app->mount(Counter::class, '/counter');
$app->group('/admin', function (Via $app): void { /* ... */ })->middleware(new AuthMiddleware());

// Plain PSR-15 handler: no context, shell or template (JSON, webhooks, MCP)
$app->route(['GET', 'POST'], '/api/items/{id}', new ItemHandler())->middleware(new ApiKeyMiddleware());
$app->route('*', '/hooks/{name}', new WebhookHandler()); // every method

// One-shot download URL for this tab's session, outside the SSE stream
$url = $c->download(function () use ($rows): \Generator {
    foreach ($rows as $row) {
        yield implode(',', $row) . "\n";
    }
}, 'rows.csv', 'text/csv; charset=utf-8');
$c->execScript('window.location = ' . json_encode($url));
```

Route parameters arrive percent-decoded; an encoded slash arrives as `/`. A `route()` request
carries `via.session`, path parameters as attributes and uploaded files; php-via checks no
Origin header there, so add CSRF or auth middleware to routes that change state. A tab keeps
its newest 100 download URLs.

---

## Scaling

### Several workers on one machine

```php
$config = (new Config())
    ->withWorkerNum(\OpenSwoole\Util::getCPUNum()); // SwooleBroker is the default with more than one worker
```

Scoped signal values, GlobalState, session data, tab state, the client list, the action rate
limit and a context directory live in shared memory. A tab lives on the worker of its SSE
stream, and an action or download that lands on another worker is passed there over the
worker pipe, at about twice the CPU of an action that lands on the tab's worker. No sticky
sessions are needed. When a tab's stream reconnects to another worker, the worker that held it
hands over the TAB signal values the browser cannot send and what its running actions send.

OpenSwoole hands each connection to one worker. Behind an h2c proxy (Caddy `h2c://`) every
client shares one upstream connection, and so one worker, until it carries 1,280 streams.
Over HTTP/1.1 (`reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000`) connections spread across workers and about
(N-1)/N of a tab's actions are passed on. Keep `withH2c()` with an HTTP/1.1 upstream: the port
answers both protocols and `withBrotli()` keeps compressing pages and streams.

What stays per worker: PHP statics in app code; server-owned TAB signals start over when the
worker that held the tab stopped. Read-modify-write on shared values loses updates between
workers: use `increment()`/`mutate()` on signals, `incrementGlobalState()`/`mutateGlobalState()`
on GlobalState, and `#[Signal(..., atomic: true)]` in the composition API. Session data and tab
state values must be serializable; tab state gets 1,024 serialized bytes per tab by default
(raise it with `withContextDirectorySize(4096, maxTabStateBytes: ...)`, 4096 being the default
row count). `withScopedSignalTableSize()`,
`withContextDirectorySize()`, `withSessionTableSize()` and `withGlobalStateTableSize()` size
the shared tables. `worker_num` in `withSwooleSettings()` that differs from `withWorkerNum()`
throws at `start()`.

A worker reload (`SIGUSR1`) keeps the shared tables, so open tabs are revived; with one worker
they reload their page. Code the master loaded before `start()`, php-via itself included,
changes only with a full restart.

### Several servers

```php
use Mbolli\PhpVia\Broker\RedisBroker;
use Mbolli\PhpVia\Broker\NatsBroker;

$config->withBroker(new RedisBroker('127.0.0.1', 6379));
$config->withBroker(new NatsBroker('127.0.0.1', 4222));
```

The broker carries broadcasts between servers. Shared memory is per machine, so contexts,
scoped signal values and GlobalState are not shared between servers: route each browser
session to one server with cookie-sticky load balancing. Servers that share a broker run the
same php-via version.

### Capacity and memory

Measured on the website with 0.14.0 (one worker, two cores at full clock, Brotli level 4): a page
view costs 1.5 to 5.8 ms of CPU with the onGrowth collector below, and 20 to 55 KB until its stream
connects or the connect timeout (30 s) passes; an open tab costs 590 to 670 KB with Brotli level 4, 75 to 145 KB at level 1 and 50
to 95 KB without Brotli, mostly the stream encoder's window; a private action 0.11 to 0.14 ms; a
broadcast about 0.05 ms per receiving tab. A broadcast to a page's scope re-renders every component
on the page, so give busy widgets a custom scope and broadcast to it, keep presence indicators out of
Scope::GLOBAL, and pass `shareRender: true` to views that are the same for every tab. A view that
returns '' on updates (`fn (bool $isUpdate) => $isUpdate ? '' : ...`) renders a static page once.
Size the shared context directory for peak open tabs plus peak page views per second times 630.
The harness is bench/capacity in the repository.

Workers keep PHP's own cycle collector runs and also run the collector every `withGcIntervalMs()`
(30 s; 0 for no timed runs). `withGcIntervalMs(30_000, onGrowth: true)` turns PHP's runs off: a worker
then runs the collector, checked every 100 ms between coroutines, when its memory has grown by half
since the last run (by 32 MiB at least, or by half the room left below `memory_limit` when that is
less), or every interval while possible roots wait. In a 250,000-view burst that is 9 runs instead of
25. A loop that creates cycles without waiting on I/O, such as a CPU-bound import in one action, then
frees them only once it ends; when they outgrow `memory_limit` first, the worker dies with a fatal
error and every tab on it with it. Use `onGrowth` only where no request runs such a loop, or call
`gc_collect_cycles()` in it. https://via.zweiundeins.gmbh/docs/performance#cycle-collector

---

## Shared and Persistent State

```php
$app->setGlobalState('motd', 'Hello');
$app->globalState('motd', 'default');
$app->incrementGlobalState('visits');                                   // atomic
$app->mutateGlobalState('log', fn (?array $l) => [...$l ?? [], $entry]); // under a lock

// Session data, per browser session
$c->setSessionData('cart', $items);
$c->sessionData('cart', []);
$app->getSessionData($request->getAttribute('via.session'), 'auth'); // in middleware

// Per-tab server values that survive a revival and a move to another worker
$c->setTabState('result', $rows);
$c->tabState('result', []);

// Keep GlobalState in SQLite across restarts (written behind, every $flushMs)
$config->withPersistentGlobalState(__DIR__ . '/state.db', flushMs: 1000);
```

With shared memory in use (`worker_num > 1` or persistence), GlobalState keys are at most
63 characters.

---

## Config Reference

Every `with*` call goes before `new Via($config)`, which freezes the Config: a later call
throws a `LogicException`. A clone of a frozen Config is not frozen.

```php
$config = (new Config())
    ->withHost('0.0.0.0')
    ->withPort(3000)                          // default 3000
    ->withTemplateDir(__DIR__ . '/templates') // Twig templates; needs composer require twig/twig
    ->withTwigCacheDir(sys_get_temp_dir() . '/twig')
    // or ->withTemplateEngine(new TwigEngine($dir, $cacheDir)), or any Rendering\TemplateEngine
    ->withShellTemplate(__DIR__ . '/shell.html')
    ->withStaticDir(__DIR__ . '/public')      // serves static files, see Static Files
    ->withDevMode(true)                       // error details, Dev Bar, warnings, no cache headers
    ->withLogLevel('info')                    // debug | info | warn | error (PSR-3 names too); others throw
    ->withBrotli()                            // pages and SSE; needs ext-brotli and withCertificate() or withH2c()
    ->withBrotli(true, 1)                     // level 1 for pages and SSE: far less memory per stream
    ->withBrotli(false)                       // no Brotli, static files included
    ->withBrotli(false, staticLevel: 11)      // Brotli for static files only
    ->withH2c()                               // HTTP/2 cleartext behind a TLS proxy; HTTP/1.1 still works
    ->withCertificate($crt, $key)             // HTTPS directly
    ->withBasePath('/app/')                   // when mounted at a sub-path
    ->withDatastarRocket()                    // Datastar + Rocket for web components
    ->withImportMap(['charts' => '/js/charts.js'], ['/js/charts.js' => 'sha384-...'])
    ->withWorkerNum(4)                        // default 1; never worker_num in withSwooleSettings()
    ->withBroker(new RedisBroker('127.0.0.1', 6379)) // several servers; SwooleBroker is the default with workers
    ->withBroadcastTickMs(25)                 // broadcast flush tick; 0 = every turn
    ->withBroadcastThrottle('import:*', 250)  // at most one render per 250 ms for matching scopes
    ->withSseKeepAliveMs(15_000)              // SSE comment on silent streams; 0 = off
    ->withSseMaxQueuedBytes(1_048_576)        // drop view frames for a slow client
    ->withContextTimeouts(
        cleanupDelayMs: 5_000,                // after a stream closes
        connectMs: 30_000,                    // free a context whose stream never connects
        reconnectMs: 60_000,                  // keep a tab whose stream is down after an action
        revivalWindowMs: 600_000,             // rebuild a returning tab
        forwardMs: 60_000,                    // wait for the worker that holds a tab, then answer 504
    )
    ->withContextDirectorySize(4096, maxTabStateBytes: 1024)
    ->withGcIntervalMs(30_000)                // timed collector runs next to PHP's; onGrowth: true replaces PHP's runs
    ->withStrictTabSignals()                  // TAB signals server-owned by default
    ->withPersistentGlobalState(__DIR__ . '/state.db')
    ->withTrustedOrigins(['https://example.com'])
    ->withAllowMissingOrigin()                // accept actions without an Origin header
    ->withActionRateLimit(100, 60)            // per IP, counted across workers
    ->withSecureCookie(true)
    ->withDevBar(false)                       // default follows devMode; on in production it is read-only
    ->withDevBarOptions(writes: false, traces: 100, pollMs: 50)
    ->withSwooleSettings(['max_request' => 10_000]) // raw OpenSwoole settings, win over php-via's
;
```

Apps read only `getBasePath()`, `isDevMode()`, `isHttps()`, `getDatastarUrl()`,
`getDatastarIntegrity()`, `getImportMap()` and `getContextRevivalWindowMs()`; the other getters
are internal. Setters renamed in 0.14 are listed under Upgrading from 0.13.

---

## Static Files

`withStaticDir()` serves a path with a file extension before routing and any other once no route
matched. A path with a segment that starts with a dot (`/.env`, `/.git/config`, `%2e` included),
except `/.well-known/`, and PHP sources (`.php`, `.php5` and other numbered forms, `.phps`, `.phpt`,
`.pht`, `.phtml`, `.phar`, `.inc`) answer 404 without a look at the disk, and so does a link in the
directory to such a file. Paths are percent-decoded, so `/my%20file.css` finds `my file.css`. Each
worker keeps files of up to 2 MiB in memory (16 MiB in all) and reads one again when it changes;
bigger files go out with `sendfile()`.

Whenever ext-brotli is loaded, compressible files (css, js, mjs, json, map, webmanifest, wasm,
svg, ico, ttf, otf, txt, md, csv, html, htm, xml, rss, atom), `/datastar.js`, `/via.css` and the
Dev Bar assets go out with Brotli level 11 to clients that accept it, with or without
`withBrotli()`, with `Vary: Accept-Encoding` and one weak ETag for every encoding. woff2, woff,
raster images (png, jpg, webp, gif, avif), pdf, audio and video are sent as they are. A worker
never compresses at level 11 itself: files of up to 128 KiB present at start are compressed in the
master process before the port opens (2.3 s at most, the website takes 0.3 s; not in dev mode) and
shared by all workers, and a helper process at the lowest CPU priority compresses bigger ones right
after start; a file that changes later goes to the helper on its first request, and until the
result arrives workers send it at level 4 up to 256 KB, uncompressed above, with
`Cache-Control: no-store`. A sidecar `foo.css.br` next to `foo.css`, at least as new, is sent as
it is, even without ext-brotli: the way to ship large assets (`brotli --best app.js`). Build
sidecars in the deploy step and keep them out of git: after a fresh clone a stale sidecar has the
same mtime as its file and counts as fresh. Memory: 32 MiB of Brotli forms from start, shared;
per worker 16 MiB uncompressed and 16 MiB of Brotli forms, 2 MiB per file; files over 8 MiB, or
whose Brotli form exceeds 2 MiB, go out uncompressed without a sidecar.

`/datastar.js?v=<hash>` (`Config::getDatastarUrl()`) is cached for a year; `via_foot` loads it.
A `withStaticCacheControl()` closure may return null to keep the default for a file.

---

## Coroutine Hooks

A worker serves all its tabs from one thread, so a blocking call stops every stream on it.
php-via sets `hook_flags` to `Via::defaultHookFlags()`: `SWOOLE_HOOK_ALL`, without
`SWOOLE_HOOK_NATIVE_CURL` on libcurl 8.20 or newer, where that hook segfaults the worker on a
curl request to any host name (curl#21558). MySQL (mysqlnd) and Redis (phpredis, predis) calls,
HTTP calls over PHP streams, file access, `sleep()`/`usleep()`, `proc_open()` and shell commands
then suspend the coroutine instead of blocking the worker. Curl requests (Guzzle's curl handlers,
Symfony's `CurlHttpClient`) suspend only under `SWOOLE_HOOK_NATIVE_CURL`, so on libcurl 8.20 or
newer each one blocks the worker until it returns. File and stdio calls go through a per-worker
thread pool: a 91 KB read costs 142 µs instead of 4.5 µs.

Never hooked, so they block the worker under any flags: pgsql/pdo_pgsql (use
`OpenSwoole\Coroutine\PostgreSQL`), SQLite, the mongodb, amqp and grpc extensions, the stat
family (`stat()`, `filemtime()`, `file_exists()`, `realpath()`), `include`, `echo` and
`error_log()`. A hooked connection must not be shared by two coroutines at once.

```php
// No file or stdio hooks, and native curl only where it does not crash (libcurl before 8.20).
// Only for apps that run no exec()/system()/popen() and hold no flock() across a suspension.
$config->withSwooleSettings(['hook_flags' => Via::noFileIoHookFlags()]);

// Cap the file thread pool: setAio(), before start(); aio_* in withSwooleSettings() fail at start-up
OpenSwoole\Util::setAio(['aio_core_worker_num' => 2, 'aio_worker_num' => 4]);
```

`start()` throws for `hook_flags` with `SWOOLE_HOOK_STDIO` but not `SWOOLE_HOOK_FILE` (includes
would suspend halfway and concurrent requests fail with "Class not found") and for a
`RedisBroker` without the socket hook it needs. The Dev Bar's Stats panel and the dev-mode `/_stats`
show the flags, the thread pool and the event loop lag. OpenSwoole 26.2 bugs: Guzzle 7.15's default
client throws on every request under `SWOOLE_HOOK_NATIVE_CURL` (use its `StreamHandler`); that
hook leaks about 2.8 KB per request with a header callback on PHP 8.4+; `mysqli_init()` plus a
failed `real_connect()` crashes the worker (use `new mysqli()` or PDO); Symfony Lock's
`FlockStore` hangs; `fsync()` returns false under the file or stdio hooks. Details:
https://via.zweiundeins.gmbh/docs/deployment#hooks

---

## Security

- `withTrustedOrigins([...])` rejects action POSTs whose `Origin` is not listed. Outside dev
  mode a POST without an `Origin` header gets 403; non-browser clients need
  `withAllowMissingOrigin()`. The Dev Bar endpoints and the tab-close beacon apply the same
  check.
- A context only accepts actions and streams from the session that created it.
- `$c->getSessionId()` and the `via.session` request attribute are a hash of the session
  cookie, never the cookie. Middleware reads the session id from `via.session`. Only cookie
  values of 32 lowercase hex characters are accepted; under `withSecureCookie(true)` only the
  `__Host-` cookie. SESSION scopes are `Scope::sessionScope($id)`, a SHA-256 hash.
- `$c->regenerateSession()` at login (and logout) gives the session a new cookie with the
  response; `$app->regenerateSession($request)` does it in middleware or a `route()` handler.
  The session id, session data and tabs stay. The session rotates at the call: the old cookie
  works for 10 more seconds, then its SSE streams end and the tabs reconnect with the new one.
  Call it before the login writes anything: it throws an `OverflowException` when the rotation
  record is full.
- CSP nonces: global middleware sets the `via.csp_nonce` request attribute; every tag of
  `via_head`, `via_foot` and the Dev Bar carries it. Datastar reads the nonce from
  `<html data-nonce="...">`; without it, it compiles expressions with `Function()`
  (`'unsafe-eval'`) and a nonce policy blocks the scripts of `execScript()` and `dispatch()`.
  The default shell writes `data-nonce` when the page request has a nonce; a custom shell
  writes `<html{{ via_html_attrs }}>`, a Twig layout `<html{{ via_html_attrs() }}>`. Both write
  nothing without a nonce and in update renders. Dev mode warns about a page with a nonce and
  no `data-nonce`.
  The middleware sends the policy as a header on the response from `$handler->handle()`, or
  the layout as `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">` in the head. Read the nonce in
  the page handler, since an action's request carries a nonce of its own.
- Headers middleware adds to the response from `$handler->handle()` go out with pages and
  actions. php-via keeps `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `Content-Encoding`,
  `Transfer-Encoding`, `Connection`, its session cookie and any header or cookie it set;
  `Vary` and `Content-Security-Policy` get both values.
- `withDevBar(true)` in production is read-only but shows every visitor's traces, scopes and
  context ids, and the server's logs and stats (`/_via/stats`), to anyone who opens a page.
- `withActionRateLimit($max, $windowSeconds)` limits actions per IP.

---

## Middleware

php-via supports PSR-15 middleware for authentication, rate limiting, CORS, etc.

```php
// Global middleware (runs on pages, actions and plain routes)
$app->middleware(new CorsMiddleware([...]));

// Per-route middleware (chained on RouteDefinition)
$app->page('/admin', $handler)->middleware(new AuthMiddleware());

// Per-group middleware
$app->group('/admin', function (Via $app) use ($handler): void {
    $app->page('/dashboard', $handler);
    $app->page('/users',     $handler);
})->middleware(new AuthMiddleware());

// In middleware: the session id, never the cookie
$sessionId = $request->getAttribute('via.session');
```

`$c->getRequestAttribute()` reads what middleware set with `$request->withAttribute()`. In an
action it is the action request's, and only global middleware runs on actions: read an
attribute from per-route middleware in the page handler and pass it to the action's closure.
A revived tab runs the route's middleware again. Implement `SseAwareMiddleware` to run on SSE
connects too.

---

## Templates

Twig is optional: `composer require twig/twig`, then `withTemplateDir()` or
`withTemplateEngine(new \Mbolli\PhpVia\Twig\TwigEngine($dir, $cacheDir))`. Without an engine,
`view('x.html.twig')`, `render()` and `getTwig()` throw with the command to run.
`Via::getTwig()` returns the Twig environment for extensions and templates held as strings
(`$app->getTwig()->createTemplate($src)->render($data)`). `Context::render()` passes the context's signals and actions to the template
by name, plus:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `contextId` | The tab's context id |
| `currentRoute` | The matched route, e.g. `/docs/signals` |
| `basePath` | Base URL path, always ends with `/` (default: `/`) |
| `via_head()` | The tags that connect the page (via_ctx, the import map, the SSE connect, the close beacon), right after `<meta charset>` |
| `via_foot()` | The Datastar module script from `Config::getDatastarUrl()`, before `</body>` |

Datastar attributes in templates, with ids written from the signal objects:
```twig
{# Display a signal value #}
<span data-text="{{ count.ref }}">{{ count.int }}</span>

{# Two-way bind an input to a signal #}
<input data-bind="{{ name.id }}" type="text">

{# Bind a web component's property: renders data-bind__prop.value="<id>" #}
<sb-slider {{ bind(volume, 'value') }}></sb-slider>

{# Trigger an action on click #}
<button data-on:click="@post('{{ increment.url }}')">+1</button>

{# Show/hide based on a signal #}
<div data-show="{{ loggedIn.ref }}">Protected content</div>
```

**Layouts and shells.** A Twig layout that renders the whole document writes
`{{ via_head() }}` right after `<meta charset>` and `{{ via_foot() }}` before `</body>`; a
closure that returns a document writes `$c->viaHead()` and `$c->viaFoot()`. A shell template
(`withShellTemplate()`) uses string placeholders, not Twig: `{{ via_head }}`, `{{ via_foot }}`,
`{{ via_html_attrs }}` (on `<html>`), `{{ head_content }}`, `{{ content }}`, `{{ foot_content }}`, `{{ base_path }}`,
`{{ context_id }}`, and `{{ name }}` / `{{ name.id }}` per signal. A layout that loads its own
Datastar bundle keeps its script, leaves out `via_foot`, and leaves `withDatastarRocket()` and
`withImportMap()` off. php-via warns once per shell or route without `via_head`. In a template
rendered outside a context, such as a `notFound()` page, `via_head()` and `via_foot()` write the
import map and the Datastar script.

---

## Web Components (Rocket, Starbase)

Rocket is Datastar's web component layer; Starbase (https://starbase.zweiundeins.gmbh) is a
catalog of Rocket components. `Config::withDatastarRocket()` makes `/datastar.js` serve
Starbase's build of Datastar 1.0.4 with Rocket (22 KB with Brotli, against 12 KB for the
plain bundle). Configure it before `new Via()`.

**One engine per page.** Components `import { rocket } from 'datastar'`, so the page needs an
import map that maps `datastar` to exactly the URL of the Datastar `<script type="module">`,
query string included, before any module script. Another URL loads a second Datastar
engine. `via_head` writes the map (with the option on, or once `withImportMap()` added
entries) and `via_foot` the script, both from `Config::getDatastarUrl()`
(`/datastar.js?v=<10 hex digits of the bundle's sha256>`). The default shell, a shell with
`{{ via_head }}`/`{{ via_foot }}` and a Twig layout with `{{ via_head() }}`/`{{ via_foot() }}`
need nothing else.

The map is an inline script: under a CSP, set the `via.csp_nonce` request attribute and
`via_head` puts the nonce on it.

**Own modules and integrity.** `Config::withImportMap(array $imports, array $integrity = [])`
merges entries into php-via's map: specifier => URL (absolute or starting with `/`; `./` and
`../` throw, since every page gets the same map), and module URL => Subresource Integrity
(`sha256-`/`sha384-`/`sha512-` + base64). Later
calls replace entries with the same key. Invalid entries and the reserved `datastar` specifier
throw `InvalidArgumentException`. `getImportMap()` returns the map. `getDatastarIntegrity()` is
the served bundle's sha384; pin Datastar with
`$config->withImportMap([], [$config->getDatastarUrl() => $config->getDatastarIntegrity()])`
after `withDatastarRocket()` and `withBasePath()`. php-via never pins it by itself: a proxy
that rewrites `/datastar.js` would break every page, since the pin covers the script tag too.
`new Via()` warns about a pin for `/datastar.js` at another URL than `getDatastarUrl()`.

**Loading components.** Take the script tag from a Starbase component page's Installation
section (pinned version with `integrity`) and add it with `$app->appendToHead(...)`. Put the
snippet's other `integrity` entries into `withImportMap()` and leave out its `datastar`
entries. To pin a whole catalog snapshot, save `https://starbase.zweiundeins.gmbh/c/@<catalog>/importmap.json`
with the app, pass its `integrity` to `withImportMap([], ...)` and load
`/c/@<catalog>/autoloader.js` with its hash from that file (93 hashes, 6 KB per page with
Brotli). Or copy the component's files into `withStaticDir()`; `.js` and `.mjs` are served as
JavaScript. A copy can get a name and its hashes with `withImportMap(['sb-qr-code' => '/vendor/starbase/qr-code@<hash>/qr-code.min.js'], [...])`,
and a page imports it with `<script type="module">import 'sb-qr-code'</script>`. Keep the version
in the folder name: a cached old file under the same URL fails the new hash.

**Binding.** Use `$signal->bind('value')` / `{{ bind(signal, 'value') }}`
(`data-bind__prop.value`) on components, and the property form for any other property
(`bind('checked')`). Plain `data-bind` binds a custom element's `value` property only if its
tag is already defined, and the `value` attribute otherwise.

**Server state.** Render the server's value into the component's attribute in the view and
post the component's `change` event to an action, which decides the value and syncs:

```twig
<sb-slider label="Thrust" value="{{ thrust.int }}" {{ bind(thrust, 'value') }}
    data-on:change="@post('{{ setThrust.url }}')"></sb-slider>
```

**Keyed lists.** The official Datastar 1.0.4 Rocket bundle crashes when a morph reorders
keyed elements that contain a Rocket component; Starbase's build fixes it, which is why
php-via serves that build.

---

## Testing

```php
use Mbolli\PhpVia\Testing\TestApp;

$app = new TestApp(new Config(), function (Via $via): void {
    $via->page('/', function (Context $c): void {
        $count = $c->signal(0, 'count');
        $c->action(fn () => $count->setValue($count->int() + 1), 'increment');
        $c->view(fn (): string => "<main id=\"counter\">{$count->int()}</main>");
    });
});
$tab = $app->open('/');            // page load plus SSE connect
$tab->patches();                   // what the stream sent so far
$tab->action('increment', ['q' => '1']);
$tab->signal('count');             // 1, the value the browser holds
$tab->html();                      // the page from server state
$tab->disconnect(expire: true);    // destroy the context; connect() or action() revives it
$app->request('GET', '/api/health'); // a plain request, to a route() or a download() URL
$app->runTasks();                  // run spawn() tasks; setInterval() timers fire meanwhile
$app->shutdown();
```

TestApp runs php-via's own request, action and SSE handlers in the test's process, with no
server, no port and no `VIA_TEST_MODE`, as one worker, with broadcasts rendered at once.
TestApp arms `$app->setInterval()` timers as worker 0 does; they and `$c->setInterval()` fire
only while `runTasks()` waits for a task or a broadcast. A test that needs an interval's work
calls it directly.

---

## Upgrading from 0.13

The full guide is https://via.zweiundeins.gmbh/docs/upgrading. The changes that break code:

- `composer require twig/twig` for `withTemplateDir()`, template views, `render()` and `getTwig()`.
- `new Via($config)` freezes the Config. Renamed setters throw and name the new call:
  `withContextCleanupDelay()`, `withContextConnectTimeout()` and `withContextRevivalWindow()` are
  `withContextTimeouts(...)`; `withTracing()` is `withDevBar()`;
  `withTracingWrites()`, `withTraceBufferSize()` and `withSsePollIntervalMs()` are
  `withDevBarOptions(...)`; `getDevMode()` is `isDevMode()`; `withGcInterval()` is
  `withGcIntervalMs()`.
- `onStart()`/`onShutdown()` are `onWorkerStart()`/`onWorkerStop()`; `config()` is `getConfig()`;
  `getContextsByScope()` is `getLocalContexts()`; `getRenderStats()` is `getStats()->getStats()`;
  `activeSseCount[$id]` is `$c->isConnected()`; `onDisconnect()`/`#[OnDisconnect]` are
  `onCleanup()`/`#[OnCleanup]`; `interval($ms, $fn)` is `setInterval($fn, $ms)`; `renderString()`
  (`$app->getTwig()->createTemplate($src)->render($data)`) and `Signal::text()` (`data-text` with
  `ref()`) are removed; `Via::parseSignals()` is gone.
- `signal()` needs a name and takes its scope as an argument; after `scope()` a signal without one
  throws. `action()` takes no scope.
- `setValue()`/`increment()`/`mutate()` take no `broadcast:`/`markChanged:`.
- `view()`: a string is a template name; `cacheUpdates:` is gone, `shareRender: true` opts into one
  render per scope.
- `component()` needs a namespace.
- Custom shells and layouts write `via_head`/`via_foot` instead of a copied bootstrap.
- `getSessionId()` and `via.session` are a hash of the cookie; SESSION scopes are per session.
- `$app->broadcast(Scope::ROUTE)` throws: `Scope::routeScope('/path')`.
- `worker_num` in `withSwooleSettings()` throws: `withWorkerNum()`.
- Datastar 1.0.4 cancels requests per method and URL, from any element.

---

## Comparisons

| Feature | php-via | Livewire | htmx + Alpine | Inertia.js | Phoenix LiveView |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Language | PHP | PHP (Laravel) | PHP (any) | PHP + JS | Elixir |
| Real-time push | ✅ SSE | ⚠️ needs Reverb | ❌ poll only | ❌ | ✅ WebSocket |
| Multiplayer scopes | ✅ built-in | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ PubSub |
| Zero JavaScript | ✅ | ❌ Alpine | ❌ Alpine/JS | ❌ React/Vue | ✅ |
| No build step | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Framework required | ❌ | Laravel | ❌ | Laravel/Symfony | Phoenix |
| Multi-worker / multi-server | ✅ Swoole / Redis / NATS | ⚠️ | N/A | N/A | ✅ |
| Persistent connection | ✅ SSE | ❌ HTTP | ❌ HTTP | ❌ HTTP | ✅ WS |

**Choose php-via when**: you want real-time multiplayer UIs in plain PHP with no
JavaScript or build tooling, or you need scoped broadcasts (route/session/global) without
an external pub/sub system.

**Choose Livewire when**: you're already in the Laravel ecosystem and don't need
server-pushed real-time without Reverb.

**Choose htmx when**: you're progressively enhancing an existing app and don't need
persistent connections or server-initiated updates.

**Choose Phoenix LiveView when**: you work in Elixir and want the original inspiration for
php-via.

---

## Common Pitfalls (Quick Reference)

1. **Hand-written signal ids**: ids include the tab and may carry a `____` suffix; write
   them from the signal object (`$signal->id()`, `$signal->ref()`, `{{ count.id }}`), never by hand.
2. **Broadcast shows stale data for other clients**: views that show shared state must read
   shared state (a scoped signal or `$app->globalState()`), not a per-client TAB signal.
3. **Dual state (globalState + Signal)**: scoped signals are already shared; use
   `$s = $c->signal(0, 'count', Scope::ROUTE)` instead of mirroring into GlobalState.
4. **Signal stays private on a shared page**: `scope()` no longer gives signals its scope; pass
   it as the third argument of `signal()`.
5. **One tab's HTML on every tab**: `shareRender: true` on a view that shows TAB signals,
   per-user data or components. Share only views that are the same for every tab.
6. **Lost updates with several workers**: `setValue($s->int() + 1)` or
   `setGlobalState($k, globalState($k) + 1)` lose writes; use `increment()`/`mutate()`.
7. **Transient state never shown**: a value set, broadcast and reset in one action never
   reaches clients, because the flush renders later; call `$app->flushBroadcasts()` first.
8. **Script runs before the morph**: `execScript()` after `broadcast()` reaches the tab
   before the broadcast frame; call `$app->flushBroadcasts()` before `execScript()`.
9. **Value frozen at page load**: compute it inside the view closure, not in the page
   handler (applies to `countClients()` and to component HTML).
10. **Variable null in view closure**: add it to both outer and inner `use` lists.
11. **Stale view after broadcast**: pass the view data as a closure, `$c->view('t', fn (): array => [...])`.
12. **PatchElementsNoTargetsFound**: the root element of your rendered view or block must have
    a unique `id` attribute. Dev mode logs a warning once per route for a page update without one.
13. **Timer fires with no clients**: guard `$app->broadcast()` with
    `if ($app->countClients($scope) === 0) return;`.
14. **Shell templates ignore Twig**: shell HTML files use string placeholders, not Twig; put
    layout logic in `{% extends %}` / `{% block %}` templates.
15. **Action returns 403**: outside dev mode, a POST without an `Origin` header, with or
    without `withTrustedOrigins()`; browsers always send one, scripts need
    `withAllowMissingOrigin()`. An `Origin` that is not in `withTrustedOrigins()`, or without
    an allowlist does not match the `Host`, gets 403 too.
16. **Rocket component fails or the page runs two Datastar engines**: enable
    `withDatastarRocket()` and write `via_head`/`via_foot` (`{{ via_head }}` in a shell,
    `{{ via_head() }}` in Twig) instead of an own map or script. Add other modules with
    `withImportMap()` instead of a second map.
17. **Two elements post the same action and one request is lost**: Datastar cancels
    in-flight requests per method and URL; add a query string (`?from=button`) or pass
    `{requestCancellation: 'disabled'}`.
18. **Dialog closes on every update**: list browser-set attributes in `data-preserve-attr`
    (`<dialog data-preserve-attr="open">`).
19. **Middleware finds no session data**: read `$request->getAttribute('via.session')`, not the
    session cookie.
20. **`Config::withX() was called after new Via()`**: make every `with*` call before
    `new Via($config)`.
